# Test: allow rays to continue THROUGH mark cells (fill bg cells along rows/cols even if interrupted by marks), then clip to not overpaint marks. Compare with demos.
def rayfill_through(I, onlybg=True):
    h,w=len(I),len(I[0]); cnt=Counter(x for r in I for x in r); bgv=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    res=[r[:] for r in I]
    def ok(i,j): return I[i][j]==bgv
    for i in range(h):
        for j in range(w):
            if not ok(i,j): continue
            for dy,dx in [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]:
                y,x=i+dy,j+dx
                while 0<=y<h and 0<=x<w:
                    if not ok(y,x): break
                    res[y][x]=3
                    y+=dy;x+=dx
                y,x=i-dy,j-dx
                while 0<=y<h and 0<=x<w:
                    if not ok(y,x): break
                    res[y][x]=3
                    y-=dy;x-=dx
    return res
for ki in [1,2,3,4]:
    I,O=G['Demo pair %d input'%ki],G['Demo pair %d output'%ki]
    bad=[(i,j,rayfill_through(I)[i][j],O[i][j]) for i in range(len(O)) for j in range(len(O[0])) if rayfill_through(I)[i][j]!=O[i][j]]
    print(ki,'match',not bad,len(bad))
